solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

parts.note: read 'currently' as 'by electric current': a device working because the power to it has been connected

explanation.surface: A question about whether something is presently up and running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Currently' looks like it means 'at present', but it really points to electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: A light or machine whose power has been connected is running, literally working by means of current.

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Testing outside a zoo-like spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TEST into a badger's burrow; 'beastly place' is a home for a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A sett is the burrow of a badger, the lair of an animal.

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is taken out of the next word

explanation.surface: Somewhere close to Winchester, the English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a tiny distance, so an inch away is barely any distance at all.

indicators.note: one piece is included inside the other

parts.note: a card is an old word for an eccentric or comic person

explanation.surface: An eccentric person was taken in by a false story.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is a false report or baseless story spread about.

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
a communication is a message

explanation.surface: An ancient letter sent from the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rome' means the Roman Catholic Church; the definition describes being expelled from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Excommunication is being cast out of the Church, so formally put out of Rome's fold.

indicators.note: an entry in something goes inside it

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
Kay is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman's name made it into the dictionary with approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To okay something is to approve it, so okayed means approved or sanctioned.

parts.note: if introduces a condition, as in 'only if'

explanation.surface: A child who has been neglected comes with some condition attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A waif is a homeless, uncared-for child, a classic picture of neglect.

parts.note: a speed marking in written music: fairly quick, in musical notes

explanation.surface: Fairly lively, and notably so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notedly' puns on 'notably' and on musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegretto is a musical tempo marking meaning moderately fast, a little slower than allegro.

clue.text: Imagine female doctor in unusual costume

parts.note: to fancy is to imagine
-ess is a suffix marking a female, as in actress

explanation.surface: Picture a woman doctor in strange clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy dress is a costume worn to dress up as someone else, out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Lab worker's hint: ice can lose shape

indicators.note: letters that lose their shape are pulled out of order and reformed, so these three words get rearranged

explanation.surface: A laboratory assistant tips off a colleague that the ice in a container is melting.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'worker's' stands for 'is', a link between the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Laboratories employ technical staff who set up and run experiments, so a lab worker is a technical assistant.

indicators.note: no here means 'without', so one piece is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: clandestine means secret or covert
to destine is to fix or settle something in advance

explanation.surface: A family that is in trouble because it has no remedy for a secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes DESTINE away from CLANDESTINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is a family group, especially a Scottish one descended from a common ancestor.

clue.text: Hated spending half minute in a vessel with Edward

indicators.note: in places the half minute inside the vessel

parts.note: a boat is a vessel

indicators.note: half of a word is its first half here

parts.note: Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Someone loathed spending thirty seconds on a boat with Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spending' joins the definition to the wordplay, suggesting time passed aboard; 'half' and 'in' are the working signals.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to loathe or detest, so abominated means hated intensely.

clue.text: Defenders to enter in close sequence

indicators.note: a piece that enters another goes inside it

parts.note: backs are defenders in football, two of them here

explanation.surface: Defenders come on to the pitch one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: Backs are defensive players in football; two of them, with TO between.
explanation.definitionFit: Events back-to-back follow one after the other without a break.

clue.text: Opening night doesn't stop being first used in importance

indicators.note: a word that does not stop has no ending, so its final letter goes

parts.note: a premiere is the opening night of a play or film

explanation.surface: A show's first night keeps on going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't stop' drops the last letter, the E. 'being' links the wordplay to the definition, which means 'first' in the sense of ranking highest.
explanation.definitionFit: Premier as an adjective means foremost or leading, ranked highest in importance.

clue.text: Pal kept getting aggravated during rousing speech

indicators.note: letters that get aggravated are stirred up and jumbled

explanation.surface: A friend became irritated during a motivational address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pep talk is a short speech meant to inspire and encourage.

clue.text: It gives high jumper an opening

definitions.text: It gives high jumper an opening

parts.words: It gives high jumper an opening
parts.note: not an athlete but a parachutist leaping from a plane, whose canopy is opened by pulling a cord

explanation.surface: Something that offers a high-jumping athlete a chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high jumper' suggests the athletics event, but it is a skydiver.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripcord is pulled to release and open a parachute.

clue.text: Left with gazetteer in Rose's place that had been burnt

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, as the clue says the left and gazetteer go in the rose's home

parts.note: a rose grows in a flower bed
an A-Z is a British street atlas, a kind of gazetteer of a city

explanation.surface: Someone takes a road atlas to the spot where a rose grew, now scorched.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-Z is the familiar British book of street maps, here giving AZ.
explanation.definitionFit: To blaze is to burn fiercely, so something that blazed was burning or had been burnt.

indicators.note: a piece that gets into another is placed inside it

parts.note: dingy means drab and shabby

explanation.surface: A man climbs aboard a rundown vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinghy is a small open boat, often a tender to a larger vessel.

clue.text: Spectacular purpose to leave no doubt

definitions.meaning: read as 'the purpose of spectacles': glasses exist to help you see things sharply
to explain something so plainly that nobody is left unsure

explanation.surface: An impressive aim is to remove all uncertainty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spectacular' is not 'impressive' here but 'to do with spectacles'.
explanation.definitionFit: Explaining fully removes confusion, and spectacles sharpen sight; both senses are the idiom about clarity.

definitions.meaning: a thin ribbon of pasta, as in a bowl of soup

explanation.surface: An idiot's lengthy portion of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is slang for a silly person and also the name of a strip of pasta.

clue.text: Ben replaced sound security device wholesale

indicators.note: replaced here means put in a new place, so the letters are reordered
sound says the word spoken aloud is what counts, not its spelling

parts.note: a lock is a security device

explanation.surface: Ben swapped out a working burglar alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges BEN to ENB; 'sound' gives LOC, which is said like LOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: En bloc means all together as one unit, so wholesale, without discrimination.

definitions.meaning: the word is used in French too, meaning free of charge, so it is its own French translation

explanation.surface: A loose rendering of a French text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free French translation' reads as a loose translation; in fact the word comes from Latin and passes unchanged into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis means given without payment, from the Latin for 'as a favour'.

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: An officer's lessons were curtailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Genera, plural of genus, are classes in biological classification.

parts.note: read literally: dough pressed and worked by hand to make a loaf, not earning a living

explanation.surface: Someone laboured to earn their living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' as slang for money suggests earning a wage; the literal sense is working dough.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread dough is pummelled and worked by hand before baking, which is exactly how it is prepared.

parts.note: tea is made from dried leaves, as in tea leaves
L is a map abbreviation for loch, a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A bird flies away from a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: the leaves of the tea plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater duck, a common bird.

parts.note: read as 'light around the head', the glowing ring painted round a saint or angel

explanation.surface: A car's front lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: Not a car lamp but light round a head.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is a ring of light shown around a holy figure's head.

indicators.note: players gathering round a table move together into a new order

parts.note: the four players at bridge are named by compass points, North, South, East and West

explanation.surface: Card players collecting secret information.
explanation.definitionFit: News is information about recent events, as intelligence is information gathered.

clue.text: I will say again one cannot read

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will
to iterate is to say or do again

explanation.surface: A speaker promises to repeat something for a person who can't read it.
explanation.definitionFit: An illiterate person is unable to read or write; the definition describes such a person.

clue.text: Some weedy keck found on mound

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some weedy cow parsley is found growing on a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'found on mound' as the definition; 'found on' is a link, and the definition is 'mound', a dyke being an earth bank. Keck is a dialect name for cow parsley.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyke can be an embankment or wall of earth, a long raised mound.

clue.text: Disgraceful Charlie took item of footwear round lousy centre

indicators.note: the footwear goes round Charlie, enclosing it

parts.note: a sandal is an open shoe with straps
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, dropping the first and last

explanation.surface: A man in a rotten pair of sandals is behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes OUS, the middle of 'lousy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandalous behaviour causes public outrage, so it is shameful.
